source.title: Towards Effective Evaluations and Comparisons for LLM Unlearning Methods
source.authors: Qi-Zhou Wang; Bo Han; Pu-Ning Yang; Jia-Ning Zhu; Tong-Liang Liu; Masashi Sugiyama

page_placements.theme: Comparing attacks and methods: fine-tuning bounds other attacks; unlearning no more robust than safety training

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses jail-breaking, embedding probing, relearning, and token noising as attacks to assess unlearning metrics. Its reported attack results concern how consistently metric scores correlate before and after attacks, not how much targeted knowledge was recovered.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ES robustness correlations under attacks, including fine-tuning unlearned models for one epoch on targeted data. Those correlations measure metric stability across setups, not the amount of knowledge restored. Its unlearning benchmarks report ES scores, not the targeted-knowledge accuracy, recovery, or prompting outcomes specified by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Jail-breaking, tuned-lens probing, one-epoch relearning and token noising are used only to pick a robust metric. Results are Pearson correlations of metric scores before and after each attack, pooled across 2 LLMs, 3 forget rates and 4 methods. These show rank stability, not how much forgotten TOFU knowledge comes back, so no version's recovery effect can be read off.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors recommend ES as the most robust metric, chiefly under relearning and probing. They propose model-mixing calibration (UWC) to compare removal at matched retention. With UWC they find tuned GA variants (GD, KL) remain strong, NPO under-unlearns and GA over-unlearns, and temperature scaling helps. They treat jail-break and probing results as the main robustness tests, because relearning and noising may alter knowledge.
record.recipe_differences: The study benchmarks several unlearning methods and uses attacks to evaluate metrics; it does not reproduce a single original unlearning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that metric robustness differs by attack: relearning and probing are more challenging than jail-breaking and token noising; ES is more robust than other candidates under relearning and probing.

fits_no_version.finding: ES PCC before/after attack (targeted/non-targeted): jail-break 0.9998/0.9999, relearn 0.7546/0.6834, probing 0.9216/0.8402, noising 0.9613/0.9729. PPL, ROUGE and EM are less stable under relearning and probing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rankings of unlearned models by memorization metrics stay stable under prompt attacks but shift under relearning and probing; ES is the most stable metric.

record.problems: The attack-robustness results report correlations rather than absolute recovery outcomes. The correlations aggregate across models, unlearning rates, and methods; numerical uncertainty for the displayed correlations is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No further claim-bearing attack rows were omitted. Other reported metrics in Figures 2 and 5 concern metric robustness rather than recovery outcomes; the unlearning benchmark tables report ES removal and retention scores, not the behaviors specified by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No targeted-accuracy-vs-chance measure, no general-capability benchmark, no absolute post-attack recovery.
Absolute knowledge restored after relearning is not reported; unrelated or loosely related relearning sets are not used.
No activation-direction ablation; no block-vs-delete analysis beyond correlations.
Jail-break recovery amounts not reported; no other languages or in-context attacks.
No method claimed to resist attacks. Tricks such as temperature scaling are judged only on calibrated ES, not attack robustness.

record.verdict_notes: Table 3 (uncalibrated) shows GA, KL and RMU driving targeted ES to about 0 while retain ES also collapses. This concerns the unlearning/retention trade-off on TOFU, not recovery of hidden knowledge, so it is not recorded as a test of A. The paper is not an original source. 'uses_without_test' with T4 fits: the attacks serve as tools for metric selection.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether targeted-knowledge accuracy reaches near chance while general ability is retained and simple attacks fail to recover knowledge.
Applies one-epoch fine-tuning on targeted data, but reports metric correlations rather than the amount of knowledge recovered; does not test unrelated or loosely related examples.
Embedding probing is used to assess metric robustness, but the paper does not ablate an activation direction or conclude that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Uses jail-breaking prompts to assess metric robustness, but does not report whether prompting restores targeted knowledge. Does not test other languages or in-context information.
Does not propose or test a counter-method for resisting the listed recovery attacks.

relation.reason: Attacks serve as a tool for metric evaluation, not as a test of any claim version.

tranche.reason: Attacks are used only to choose a robust unlearning metric. The study reports no recovery of forgotten knowledge.

source_check.notes: Figure 2's panel layout is garbled in the text. Figure 5 (appendix) places the ES row as jail 0.9942/0.9838, relearn 0.7546/0.6834, probing 0.9216/0.8402, noising 0.9613/0.9729. 0.9998/0.9999 is PPL noising, close to KL noising 0.9999/1.0000, as the text's 'PPL and KL are very similar' leads one to expect. The values are PCCs of metric scores, not amounts of knowledge recovered.

statements.correction: ES Pearson correlation (PCC) of metric scores before/after attack (targeted/non-targeted), pooled over Phi-1.5 and Llama-2-7B on TOFU, 1/5/10% forgetting, GA/GD/PO/NPO: jailbreak 0.9942/0.9838, relearn 0.7546/0.6834, probing 0.9216/0.8402, noising 0.9613/0.9729. These measure metric robustness, not knowledge recovered.
statements.problem: The jailbreak pair 0.9998/0.9999 is the PPL token-noising panel. ES under jail-breaking is 0.9942/0.9838. The other three ES pairs are right. The measure is Pearson (linear) correlation, not rank correlation. The values are pooled over 2 LLMs, 3 forget rates and 4 methods.
